marks.q: We remain on track to deliver full year 2021 results in line with our previous guidance. We will continue to prioritise operating margin*†, our primary performance measure, and remain on track to deliver an operating margin target of c.21-22% in the medium term.

The business performed very well in the year and we will report 2021 full year results in line with expectations1, with significant improvement in operating margin, as we focused on optimising sales prices, alongside increased volume, driving strong growth in operating profit
Trading is in line with expectations and we remain on track to deliver against our guidance set out at our 2021 full year results in March.
Guidance for operating margin and outlet-led volume growth is reconfirmed today.

Looking ahead, we expect full year Group operating profit to be around the top end of the current market consensus range driven by strong average selling prices on completions that are expected to be 4-5% higher than last year.

With resilient pricing in the order book and a focus on cost discipline, we expect to deliver operating profit in line with our expectations. We expect Group volumes to be at broadly similar levels to 2021, given the uncertainty in the market.
Accordingly, we enter 2023 with a lower private order book than in recent years and we expect overall volumes to reduce in 2023.

Accordingly, assuming prevailing market conditions continue and given a challenging planning backdrop, we currently expect 2023 completions to be in the range of 9,000 to 10,500, broadly equivalent to a net sales rate assumption of 0.5 to 0.7, with completions more weighted to the second half, reflecting the lower sales rate since Q3 2022.

We continue to expect 2023 completions to be in the range of 9,000 to 10,500, broadly equivalent to an annual net sales rate assumption of 0.5 to 0.7, with completions more weighted to the second half.

We expect full year UK completions excluding joint ventures to be in the range of 10,000 to 10,500, at the upper end of our previous guidance and we expect Group operating profit including joint ventures to be in the range of £440 million to £470 million.
Due to our focus on optimising price and sharp cost discipline, we now expect Group operating profit* to be at the top end of our guidance range of £440 million to £470 million.
We continue to expect full year Group operating profit to be at the top end of our guidance range of £440 million to £470 million.

Accordingly, and given prevailing market conditions, we remain focused on optimising value and currently expect 2024 UK completions (excluding JVs) to be in the range of 9.5k to 10k homes, with completions weighted 45 / 55% in favour of the second half of the year.
We continue to expect 2024 UK completions (excluding JVs) to be in the range of 9,500 to 10,000, with completions weighted 45% / 55% in favour of the second half of the year.

Looking to the second half, our performance to date means we now expect to deliver 2024 full year UK completions towards the upper end of our previous guidance range of 9,500 to 10,000 and Group operating profit in line with current market expectations.1

We continue to expect to deliver full year 2024 UK volumes excluding JVs towards the upper end of our guidance range of 9,500 to 10,000 homes, and to deliver Group operating profit in line with current market expectations1.

Whilst price negotiations for 2025 are ongoing, we anticipate increased build cost pressure as a result of the changed economic backdrop, including as suppliers seek to factor in the impacts of the recent UK Budget.
We expect to deliver full year 2025 UK completions in the range of 10,400 to 10,800 excl. JVs and for Group performance to be in line with market expectations1.
We continue to expect 2025 Group operating profit to be in line with our previous guidance1.

As a result of the £20.0 million unexpected charge booked in H1 2025, associated with historical defective workmanship by a principal contractor, the Group now expects to deliver operating profit for 2025 of c.£424 million.

We remain on track to deliver our full year 2025 guidance range of 10,400 to 10,800 UK completions (excluding JVs) and we continue to expect to deliver full year Group operating profit* of c.£424 million.

We continue to expect to deliver full year 2025 UK completions and Group operating profit* in line with our previous guidance1, and remain on track to close out the year operating from 210-215 outlets as previously guided.

Taking these factors into account, we expect Group operating profit margin to be lower in 2026 than in 2025 and, given the lower opening order book, for performance to be more second half weighted in 2026 than in prior years.

As previously guided, Group adjusted operating profit margin for 2026 is expected to be lower than 2025, reflecting softer pricing in the order book coming into the year together with continued low single digit build cost inflation. Therefore, we expect 2026 adjusted operating profit to be around £400 million1.
As a result of rising energy costs, build cost inflation is now expected to be low to mid single digit for 2026, with cost pressure and surcharges starting to come through from our supply chain.

Reflecting the prolonged nature of the downturn which has reduced expected profitability and cash generation, the Board has reviewed the level of cash returns and deemed it prudent to revise our Distribution Policy to preserve balance sheet strength, retain financial flexibility and support our commitment to optimising shareholder returns through the cycle.
